title: Grateful Dead Live at Electric Theater on 1969-04-25

ai_review.summary: Top‑shelf Charlie Miller soundboard transfer of a brief but vibrant April ’69 Chicago set, highlighted by Pigpen’s powerhouse Schoolgirl and Garcia’s slide on Hard to Handle.
ai_review.review: This recording offers an excellent soundboard capture that lets listeners hear the raw energy of a short early‑'69 show. Pigpen dominates with a fiery Good Morning Little Schoolgirl and other blues‑heavy numbers, while Jerry Garcia adds memorable slide work on Hard to Handle and drives the jams on Doin’ That Rag and Morning Dew. The set is brief and missing its second half, but the performance quality and transfer fidelity make it a valuable snapshot of the Dead’s evolving sound.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise both the musical performance (average show‑related rating ~4.2) and the transfer quality (5 stars for the Charlie Miller soundboard). Weighted combination yields a strong 4.3 overall.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Charlie Miller's meticulous transfer chain (Sony R500 → Sound Devices 744T → Adobe Audition → Samplitude → FLAC) results in crystal‑clear, well‑balanced audio with no noted dropouts or distortion.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A concise ~1‑hour set dominated by Pigpen’s vocals and blues jams. The early‑'69 material feels raw and electric, transitioning toward the folk‑psychedelia that would emerge later; a promised second set is missing, leaving the recording feeling incomplete.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia delivers slide guitar on Hard to Handle and adds a distinctive G accent at the end of Doin' That Rag, driving the jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil's bass work is praised as solid and “at their very best,” anchoring the blues‑heavy set.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drummers are noted for being at their very best, providing a tight, propulsive rhythm throughout.
